consolidation.note: Single canonical, runtime-queryable tool registry for Darkly. Supersedes darkly_tools_registry.json, darkly_money_freedom_registry.json, and darkly_tool_directory.json — this file is their fully merged, deduplicated, validated union. Load this file only.

source_files_merged.role: flattened directory of base registry only (superseded, not needed once this file exists)
prior merged directory (base for this fix)

fixes_applied: Normalized 254 tools with missing `permission` to explicit "unspecified" (previously null, but already bucketed as "unspecified" in the index — now the tool object and index agree).
Added a self-contained `tags` array to 659 tools that were tagged in the index but did not carry their own `tags` field, so tags can be read directly off a tool without cross-referencing the index.
Rebuilt by_id/by_section/by_permission/by_status/by_tag/by_registry indices from scratch off the corrected tool list (previous indices were already accurate — this just guarantees it post-fix).
Recomputed all counts from the tool list directly rather than carrying forward prior counts.
Verified zero duplicate ids across all 960 tools and zero orphaned index references.

query_guide.note: Read this once at load time; everything below is how to query this file in-process without re-scanning `tools`.
query_guide.lookup_by_id: index.by_id[<id>] -> integer position in `tools`; tools[position] is the full record.
query_guide.filter_by_section: index.by_section[<section>] -> list of ids in that section (e.g. 'markets_and_investing', 'device_capability').
query_guide.filter_by_permission: index.by_permission[<permission>] -> list of ids. Values: read, local_execution, internal_write, external_write, external_communication, financial_action, device_permission_or_read, unspecified.
query_guide.filter_by_status: index.by_status[<status>] -> list of ids. Many distinct status strings exist (e.g. candidate, verified_existing, concept_specification_not_verified_build) — treat as free-form provenance, not a fixed enum.
query_guide.filter_by_registry: index.by_registry[<registry_key>] -> list of ids from that source registry (darkly_tools_registry_v2 or darkly_money_freedom_registry_v1).
query_guide.before_using_a_tool: Check `permission` on the tool record against `safety_model` and `autonomy_policy` below before calling it — anything above `read`/`local_execution` needs the corresponding authorization per autonomy_policy.financial_action_requirements (for financial_action) or the general external_write/external_communication gating.
query_guide.merge_conflicts: A tool may carry a `_merge_conflicts` object if the two source registries disagreed on a field (e.g. `kind` or `category`); the value actually kept is the top-level field, and `_merge_conflicts` records what the other registry said, for transparency only.

safety_model.local_execution: May run isolated analysis/calculation with resource limits.
safety_model.internal_write: May change Darkly-owned state, models, notes, forecasts, ledgers, and research records.
safety_model.external_write: May alter an outside system only within an explicitly authorized scope.
safety_model.external_communication: May contact third parties only within an explicitly authorized communication policy.
safety_model.financial_action: May move money, create financial obligations, trade, refund, pay, or issue value only under explicit execution policy and hard limits.

safety_model_note: Union of both source registries' safety models; darkly_money_freedom_registry_v1's definitions are used as canonical since they add local_execution and are more explicit. See 'registries' for original wording.

loading_rules.credentials: Resolve credential_env names from environment variables or a secret manager.
loading_rules.registry_version_notes: v2 expands beyond network APIs so Darkly can distinguish local executables, runtime libraries, device sensors, cloud/platform services, internal engines, and retired/historical integrations.

autonomy_policy.principle: Broad autonomy for reading, researching, browsing, calculating, simulating, reconciling, and challenging conclusions; explicit policy gates for external writes, communications, and financial actions.

orchestration_rules.rule: Classify every money question into one or more domains before selecting tools.
Prefer first-party account data, regulators, official filings, official economic data, and primary merchant/accounting records over secondary summaries when available.
For high-impact financial decisions, seek corroboration from independent sources and surface disagreement.
Use deterministic calculators/code for arithmetic, tax formulas, amortization, portfolio math, valuation, optimization, and scenario analysis instead of freehand estimates when inputs are available.
Preserve as-of timestamps and never use future data in historical evaluation or backtesting.
Do not mix cash-flow conclusions with accrual accounting without an explicit reconciliation.
Distinguish nominal returns/values from inflation-adjusted real returns/values.
Prefer net-after-fee, net-after-tax, and net-after-friction outcomes when judging real economic value.
Never compare returns without considering risk, liquidity, duration, taxes, fees, and capital lockup.
Every capital allocation can be compared against relevant alternatives and the cost of doing nothing.
Represent forecasts as ranges/distributions when uncertainty is material, not fake point precision.
Do not claim money moved, a trade filled, payroll ran, a refund occurred, or an invoice was sent without returned confirmation from the action system.
